summary: Reviewed all 36 sources, 119 evidence items, and 63 entities (22 companies, 23 facilities, 14 flows, 4 financial_links; 0 controls in this layer) in data/research/materials.json. Verdicts: 46 publish, 16 publish_flagged, 1 reject (flow:hemlock-to-shin-etsu-polysilicon). Every quote was checked against the primary document: USGS PDFs and company/regulatory web pages were fetched directly with a declared, non-email project User-Agent; SEC.gov blocked direct curl fetches of all four filings (mp-8k, mp-10k, corning-10k, teck-aif) as an "undeclared automated tool" even with a compliant UA, so those were instead verified via EDGAR full-text search (efts.sec.gov), confirming every quoted phrase as a unique verbatim hit inside the exact cited accession number -- this is as reliable as opening the file directly, since EDGAR indexes the filing's own text. regulations.gov (downloads.regulations.gov) CloudFront-blocked the GlobalWafers BIS docket attachment via both curl and a fetch tool; that one quote is corroborated only via a search-engine index reproducing the exact sentence and document title, and is flagged reachable=false -- it is not load-bearing for any entity verdict. The Lynas FY26 ASX API URL was checked to actually resolve to a genuine, correctly-dated 141-page encrypted PDF (not just an HTTP 200), and its content matches. Two systemic issues were corrected: (1) the five USGS "country aggregate" companies for China had names that read as if they were real corporate entities ("China primary gallium producers", etc.); all five were renamed to an unambiguous "China — <commodity> (USGS aggregate)" pattern and marked publish_flagged, though their underlying production-share figures are all Tier-1 verified verbatim. (2) The SIA and GlobalWafers comments filed in the BIS Section 232 polysilicon docket were classed regulatory_filing/Tier 1; both are reassigned to Tier 2 in source_checks, because they are industry advocacy submissions self-reporting market structure, not a government determination -- the fact that a document sits inside an official federal docket does not make its content a Tier-1 government finding. This does not break publish status for anything relying on them, since the evidence standard only requires Tier 1/2, not Tier 1 specifically, for any entity here. Of the five wafer-maker flows inferred from "Wacker supplies all major wafer manufacturers" + a named wafer maker on the SIA five-supplier list, four (Shin-Etsu, Sumco, GlobalWafers, SK Siltron) are sound two-fact inferences of the kind AGENTS.md itself models (general claim + named party in that category) and are publish_flagged as inferred. The fifth, flow:hemlock-to-shin-etsu-polysilicon, is REJECTED: it rests on joint-venture co-ownership alone with no affirmative supply-relationship claim from either party (unlike Wacker, Hemlock never describes its own customer base), which is exactly the kind of ownership-only inference the brief warns should not stand on its own. By contrast, flow:orbia-las-cuevas-to-matamoros-hf is accepted as publish_flagged: both sites are wholly owned/operated by the same integrated Orbia business unit (not merely co-owned by a third party), and the company affirmatively describes "fully integrated operations, from raw material extraction to chemical processing," which is a materially stronger basis than ownership alone. teck-aif-2025's doc_type is mislabeled sec_20f (it is actually Exhibit 99.1 to a Form 40-F, since Teck is a Canadian MJDS filer) -- flagged doc_type_ok=false in source_checks; tier remains 1. fac:orbia-matamoros-hf is publish_flagged because its 30,000 t/yr HF capacity figure is undated at the source (already disclosed by the analyst in the capacity note). No other correction, quote problem, or unsupported claim was found: MP Materials' DoD figures (M preferred equity, up to M more, M loan, /kg NdPr floor, the 10-year/10X-Facility DoD offtake) all check out verbatim against the 8-K, and the Lynas "will no longer proceed" Seadrift-cancellation quote is exact. The analyst's gaps[] section is honest and appropriately conservative -- nothing there should have been asserted as a documented claim.
